home.heroTitle: Hydrological calculations with verified IDF data
home.heroSubtitle: Calculate design discharges using intensity-duration-frequency data from official Argentine sources.
home.heroDescription: Calculate design discharges using IDF data from official Argentine sources: APA Chaco, INA-CRA, SsRH Neuquén, UTN-ER, UNL, INA-CIRSA, INTA, UNT-FACET. Rational Method, SCS-CN, Tc formulas, Manning and culverts.
home.localitiesSubtitle: 18 localities in 11 provinces. Sources: APA (Chaco/Formosa), INA-CRA (Mendoza/Catamarca), SsRH Neuquén, UTN Concordia, UNL, INA-CIRSA (Córdoba/Salta), INTA (Buenos Aires), UNT-FACET (Tucumán).
home.moreLocalities: New localities will be added as official sources are verified.
home.viewFullDetails: View full details and IDF tables →
home.calculatorsSubtitle: Integrated hydrological and hydraulic calculation tools.
home.methodologyText: AutoHydro implements standard hydrological engineering methods: Rational Method, SCS-CN (USDA), 6 Time of Concentration formulas, Manning equation and culvert sizing according to FHWA HDS-5. IDF data come exclusively from verified official sources.
home.disclaimerText: This tool generates estimates for preliminary design stages. For final designs, always verify with the most recent local hydrological studies.
home.disclaimerFull: This tool generates estimates for preliminary design stages. For final designs, always verify with the most recent local hydrological studies and applicable provincial regulations.
home.toolHydrologyDesc: Design discharges using Rational Method and SCS-CN. Tc analysis, CN and PDF report generation.
home.toolManningDesc: Open channel capacity: trapezoidal, rectangular, circular and triangular.
home.toolCulvertsDesc: Culvert sizing per FHWA HDS-5: inlet and outlet control.
home.toolHyetogramDesc: Design storm with temporal distribution: Alternating Blocks, SCS Type II, Chicago, Uniform.

about.title: About AutoHydro Argentina
about.pageSubtitle: AutoHydro Argentina — open source hydrological calculation tool.
about.developerBio: Civil engineer with experience in hydrology and hydraulics. Worked at the Provincial Water Administration (APA) of Chaco in hydrological studies and urban stormwater drainage design.
about.projectText1: AutoHydro Argentina is an open source hydrological calculation tool for professional practice in Argentina. The included IDF data covers 18 localities in 11 provinces and comes from verified sources: APA (Chaco), UTN-ER / Dirección de Hidráulica (Entre Ríos), UNL-CURIHAM (Santa Fe), IHLLA-CONICET (Buenos Aires), INTA (Buenos Aires), INA-CIRSA (Córdoba and Salta), INA-CRA (Mendoza and Catamarca), SsRH (Neuquén) and UNT-FACET (Tucumán).
about.projectText2: The project incorporates 9 different IDF models to accommodate the methodological diversity of Argentine sources. New localities are added only when data from verifiable technical publications is available: official resolutions, peer-reviewed papers, and technical reports from water authorities.
about.contactText: Found a bug, have a suggestion, or want to collaborate? Open an issue on GitHub or contact me directly on LinkedIn.

manning.subtitle: Open channel flow capacity
manning.materialHint: To verify admissible erosion and sedimentation velocities.
manning.designCheckHint: Enter the design flow from the hydrological analysis to verify if the channel has sufficient capacity.
manning.emptyState: Fill in the parameters and press "Calculate Manning"
manning.flowFromCalcBadge: Design flow pre-loaded from hydrological analysis
manning.regimeSubcritical: Flow is controlled downstream. Suitable for irrigation and drainage channels.
manning.regimeCritical: Unstable condition — small disturbances cause large variations. Avoid in design.
manning.regimeSupercritical: Fast flow controlled upstream. Requires energy dissipation at channel end.
manning.regimePressure: Conduit works under pressure. Verify sealing and anchors.

validation.nRequired: Enter a valid Manning n coefficient (> 0).

culvert.pageSubtitle: Inlet and outlet control · Argentine commercial sizes
culvert.insufficientDesc: HW/D = {{ratio}} exceeds the physical limit of 4.0. The section cannot convey this flow. A larger culvert, multiple barrels, or a bridge is required.
culvert.hwNearLimit: HW/D = {{ratio}} — near the recommended limit. Consider a larger section.
culvert.hwMaxNote: ✓ = computed HW ≤ max. allowable HW ({{hwmax}} m)
culvert.methodologyText1: Calculation based on FHWA HDS-5 (Hydraulic Design of Highway Culverts). Headwater (HW) is computed under inlet and outlet control; the governing (larger) value is adopted.
culvert.methodologyInlet: Inlet control: limited by the inlet capacity (FHWA nomograph, polynomial approximation).
culvert.methodologyOutlet: Outlet control: energy equation with inlet losses (Ke), friction (Manning–Darcy) and outlet velocity.
culvert.methodologyNote: Commercial sizes per Argentine practice (IRAM/CIRSOC). For final designs, verify with provincial standards and construction drawings.
culvert.flowFromCalcBadge: Design flow pre-loaded from hydrological analysis

idfStep.title: IDF Source — City and return period

alternating_blocks.label: Alternating Blocks
alternating_blocks.desc: Most widely used method in Argentina. Distributes rainfall blocks symmetrically around the central peak.

scs_type_ii.label: SCS Type II
scs_type_ii.desc: USDA-NRCS dimensionless distribution for humid regions (NEA, Pampa Húmeda). Peak at 70% of duration.

chicago.label: Chicago (r = 0.4)
chicago.desc: Asymmetric storm with peak at 40% of total duration. Common in Argentine urban studies.

uniform.label: Uniform
uniform.desc: Constant intensity equal to the IDF value for total duration. Conservative and simple.

validation.timeStepExceedsDuration: Time step (Δt) cannot exceed total duration.
